messages.subject_clean: Course: Online. Sex Chromosome Evolution. 12-16 October
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

there are still a few seats left for our online course on Sex Chromosome Evolution

 
Dates: 12?16 October 
 
Course website: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/sexchr/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/sexchr/ ) 
 
How do sex chromosomes evolve, and what can genomic and transcriptomic data tell us about their differentiation?
 
This hands-on online course will introduce practical approaches for identifying sex chromosomes and studying their evolution. Across five live sessions, we?ll work with genomic and transcriptomic data to explore recombination suppression, evolutionary strata, sex-biased gene expression, dosage compensation, gene gain and loss, and genome divergence.
 
The course combines short lectures with practical computational exercises using Linux command-line tools and R and Bioconductor. Participants will work with real datasets and learn how to analyse and interpret genomic patterns in an evolutionary context.
 
For the full list of our courses and workshops, please visit: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/ )
 
 
 
Best regards,
Carlo


--------------------

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Writing Your First Paper (Free Seminar) - Genetic research writing
messages.subject_clean: Writing Your First Paper (Free Seminar) - Genetic research writing
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Careful manuscript choices can make genetic evidence easier to evaluate and reuse. Writing Your First Paper (Free Seminar) is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 5?6 with Jenifer Lopes (Department of Organismic & Evolutionary Biology, Faculty of Arts & Sciences, Harvard University). Communicate genetic analyses with a clear account of hypotheses, methods, results, and their contribution. Build literature searches and citation strategies that locate R-based genetic work within relevant debates. Learn journal selection, abstract writing, and ethical AI-assisted editing practices for a publication-ready manuscript.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/writing-your-first-paper-free-seminar
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director
Instats | instats.org

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Multilevel and Mixed Models for Genetics
messages.subject_clean: Multilevel and Mixed Models for Genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Hierarchical genetic datasets call for explicit attention to dependence. Multilevel and Mixed Models with AI is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 7 and 9 with Michael Zyphur (Instats | instats.org). Specify multilevel models for genetic data structured by families, populations, sites, or repeated measurements. Estimate random effects and multilevel path models in R and Mplus while separating sources of variation. Use diagnostics, simulation, and carefully documented AI assistance to support transparent genetic analyses.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/multilevel-and-mixed-models-with-ai
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director
Instats | instats.org
